card.name: Dosing and risk phrases in labels
card.fires_on: Varied words inside dosing tables, trial statistics and preparation instructions in drug labels, such as 'mL' after a number, 'risk' after 'absolute', or 'Injection' after sodium chloride. The common thread is a word in the middle of a quantity or dose phrase.

modes.label: Units and forms in dosing
modes.description: A unit or product-form word right after an amount or ingredient name in dose and preparation text.

modes.label: Absolute risk in trial results
modes.description: The word 'risk' after 'The absolute' in hormone-therapy dementia statistics.
modes.example: The absolute<< risk>> of probable dementia for CE-alone versus placebo

modes.label: Linking words in dose instructions
modes.description: Small connecting words such as 'or', 'under', 'times' or 'in' inside dose or administration sentences.
modes.example: administer as directed<< under>> the Administration Instructions below
